revision_signal: verbal self-reflection after episode failure (binary/scalar env feedback)
role_in_survey: foundation: episodic reflective memory as text-based revision signal
note: Agent writes natural-language reflections on failed trials into an episodic memory buffer reused in later attempts; no weight updates. 91% pass@1 on HumanEval.
title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning

revision_signal: observation stream; periodic reflection triggered by importance threshold
role_in_survey: foundation: memory stream + reflection + planning architecture
note: Memory stream of natural-language observations retrieved by recency/importance/relevance and synthesised into higher-level reflections that drive planning; 25-agent sandbox with ablations showing observation, planning, reflection each matter.
title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior

revision_signal: self-directed memory paging via function calls; interrupts
role_in_survey: foundation: OS-style tiered memory managed by the LLM itself
note: LLM manages main context vs external storage tiers through explicit memory read/write functions (virtual context management); evaluated on document analysis beyond context length and multi-session chat consistency.
title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems

revision_signal: environment execution feedback, errors, self-verification
role_in_survey: foundation: skill library as procedural memory plus iterative prompting
note: Automatic curriculum, growing code skill library, and iterative prompting with execution feedback/self-verification in Minecraft; 3.3x more unique items, 2.3x longer distances, tech-tree milestones up to 15.3x faster.
title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models

revision_signal: success detection, scene description, human feedback injected into prompt
role_in_survey: foundation: closed-loop textual feedback as state update for embodied LLM planners
note: Environment feedback (success detectors, object/scene descriptions, human responses) is appended into the LLM's prompt as an inner monologue enabling replanning; improves long-horizon completion in simulated and real kitchen tasks.
title: Inner Monologue: Embodied Reasoning through Planning with Language Models

revision_signal: affordance value functions score skill feasibility
role_in_survey: foundation: grounding LLM plans in affordance values; open-loop baseline for later feedback work
note: Combines LLM likelihood of a skill with a learned value function estimating feasibility to pick each step; no explicit belief maintenance, open-loop w.r.t. state. Real mobile manipulator long-horizon tasks.
title: Do As I Can, Not As I Say: Grounding Language in Robotic Affordances

revision_signal: conceptual: learning actions update memory modules
role_in_survey: foundation: taxonomy of memory modules (working/episodic/semantic/procedural) and decision cycle
note: Conceptual framework organising language agents by modular memory, structured action space (internal vs external), and a decision loop; retrospective survey of existing agents.
title: Cognitive Architectures for Language Agents

revision_signal: LLM-as-world-model predicted next states plus task reward in MCTS
role_in_survey: foundation: LLM as explicit world model for planning (state predicted in text)
note: LLM repurposed as world model predicting next state and as reasoning agent; MCTS over the reasoning tree. LLaMA-33B with RAP beats CoT on GPT-4 by 33% relative in plan generation.
title: Reasoning with Language Model is Planning with World Model

revision_signal: self-evaluation of intermediate thoughts; backtracking
role_in_survey: foundation: deliberate search over thought states with self-evaluation
note: Generalises CoT to tree search where the LM generates and evaluates intermediate thoughts with lookahead/backtracking; Game of 24 success 74% vs 4% for GPT-4 CoT.
title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models

decision: exclude(no state or belief maintenance; single-turn tool use)
revision_signal: n/a
role_in_survey: background: self-supervised API-call learning; tool use as evidence acquisition
note: Model self-annotates API calls (calculator, search, QA) and is fine-tuned on those that reduce loss; improves zero-shot performance but no sequential state tracking.
title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools

revision_signal: self-generated natural-language feedback on own output
role_in_survey: foundation: iterative self-feedback loop without external signal
note: Same LM generates output, critiques it, and refines iteratively with no training; about 20% absolute improvement averaged over seven tasks with GPT-3.5/ChatGPT/GPT-4.
title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback

revision_signal: LLM-sampled world state belief (object locations) plus LLM policy prior in MCTS
belief_level_metrics: partial (belief sampled from LLM as commonsense prior over object locations)
role_in_survey: foundation: LLM as commonsense belief prior over world state for MCTS
note: Uses the LLM both as a commonsense world model (sampling initial belief over object locations) and as heuristic policy inside MCTS for household tasks; outperforms MCTS alone and GPT-3.5 policies by a wide margin on complex novel tasks.
title: Large Language Models as Commonsense Knowledge for Large-Scale Task Planning

revision_signal: descriptor of execution outcome; self-explanation of failure
role_in_survey: foundation: describe-explain-plan loop for open-world replanning
note: Plans are iteratively refined via a descriptor summarising execution and an explainer diagnosing failure, plus a learned selector ranking sub-goals; first zero-shot agent on 70+ Minecraft tasks, roughly doubling performance.
title: Describe, Explain, Plan and Select: Interactive Planning with Large Language Models Enables Open-World Multi-Task Agents

revision_signal: n/a (benchmark)
role_in_survey: foundation: multi-environment agent benchmark; outcome-level metrics only
note: Eight interactive environments for evaluating LLMs as agents; finds open-source models below 70B lag far behind commercial LLMs with long-term reasoning and instruction following as bottlenecks.
title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents

revision_signal: n/a (benchmark)
role_in_survey: foundation: multimodal web-agent benchmark with outcome-based evaluation
note: Benchmark of realistic visually grounded web tasks; text-only LLM agents struggle and current multimodal agents show large gaps.
title: VisualWebArena: Evaluating Multimodal Agents on Realistic Visual Web Tasks

revision_signal: n/a (environment)
role_in_survey: foundation: partially observable text environment used by ReAct/Reflexion/ExpeL
note: Aligns TextWorld with ALFRED embodied tasks so text-learned policies (BUTLER) transfer to visual execution; standard partially observed testbed for later LLM agents.
title: ALFWorld: Aligning Text and Embodied Environments for Interactive Learning

revision_signal: return-to-go conditioning over past state-action history
role_in_survey: foundation: sequence-modelling view of control; history-in-context as implicit state
note: Casts offline RL as autoregressive sequence modelling conditioned on desired return, past states and actions; matches or exceeds model-free offline RL baselines on Atari, Gym, Key-to-Door.
title: Decision Transformer: Reinforcement Learning via Sequence Modeling

revision_signal: n/a (probing)
role_in_survey: foundation: false-belief probing of LLM belief attribution
note: 640 false-belief prompts over 40 tasks; GPT-4 solves 75%, comparable to six-year-olds, older models fail; framed as emergent ToM.
title: Evaluating Large Language Models in Theory of Mind Tasks

revision_signal: foresee-and-reflect structured prompting from inferred mental states
belief_level_metrics: partial (belief tracking accuracy vs action selection on T4D)
role_in_survey: foundation: gap between tracking others' beliefs and acting on them
note: T4D benchmark shows GPT-4 tracks beliefs well but fails to select actions; FaR zero-shot prompting raises GPT-4 from 50% to 71% on T4D and generalises OOD.
title: How FaR Are Large Language Models From Agents with Theory-of-Mind?

revision_signal: dialogue history plus schema descriptions; state regenerated each turn
role_in_survey: foundation: pre-LLM-agent belief-state tracking with explicit slot-value state
note: Generative T5 DST with schema-driven prompts encoding task-aware history; SOTA on MultiWOZ 2.2 and competitive on 2.1 and M2M; belief state as explicit slot-value object.
title: Dialogue State Tracking with a Language Model using Schema-Driven Prompting

revision_signal: n/a (translate to PDDL, symbolic planner)
role_in_survey: foundation: externalising state to a symbolic planner representation
note: LLM translates NL problem into PDDL, classical planner solves, LLM translates back; produces optimal plans for most benchmark problems while bare LLMs fail to give feasible plans.
title: LLM+P: Empowering Large Language Models with Optimal Planning Proficiency

revision_signal: recursive self-criticism of proposed action against task and state
role_in_survey: foundation: self-critique loop for computer-control actions
note: Recursive Criticism and Improvement prompting critiques and revises output at task, state and agent grounding levels; SOTA on MiniWoB++ with a handful of demos per task, beating SL and RL baselines.
title: Language Models can Solve Computer Tasks

revision_signal: cross-task insight extraction from success/failure trajectories
role_in_survey: foundation: cross-task experiential memory of natural-language insights
note: Collects trajectories, extracts insights by comparing successes and failures, retrieves insights and similar experiences at inference without parameter updates; performance grows with experience and transfers across tasks.
title: ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners

revision_signal: Ebbinghaus-style forgetting with time decay and importance; user-portrait updating
role_in_survey: foundation: long-term conversational memory with forgetting dynamics
note: Long-term memory store with retrieval, continual updating, and Ebbinghaus-inspired forgetting; demonstrated in the SiliconFriend companion with improved recall and personality understanding.
title: MemoryBank: Enhancing Large Language Models with Long-Term Memory

revision_signal: LLM rewrites its own natural-language short-term and long-term memory each step
role_in_survey: foundation: language-based recurrent state written by the model
note: Simulates an LSTM in natural language: each step the LLM outputs a paragraph plus updated short-term memory and stores long-term memory on disk; interpretable and editable, used for long-text generation.
title: RecurrentGPT: Interactive Generation of (Arbitrarily) Long Text
